title_en: Ji Pin v. Yicheng Police Station of Yixing Public Security Bureau — dispute over other administrative acts in public security
ruling_gist_en: When an administrative agency applies a catch-all clause, it should be associated with the situations already explicitly enumerated in the same clause, and refer to the standards set for those explicitly enumerated situations to determine whether the catch-all clause can be applied. The situations to which the catch-all clause applies shall have the same or similar value as the situations already explicitly enumerated in the same clause, be consistent in terms of nature and degree of impact, and comply with the legislative purpose of that clause.
keywords_en: Administration; Public security administrative penalty; Second instance; Intermediate People's Court; Jiangsu Province; Natural person; State organ; Provisions on the Procedure for Public Security Organs Handling Administrative Cases; Conditions for application of catch-all clause; Whether insufficient evidence constitutes a ground for termination of investigation; Affirm the original judgment; Public security case; Insufficient evidence; Expiration of case-handling period; Termination of investigation; Administrative litigation; Administrative penalty
full_text_en:
Ji Pin v. Yicheng Police Station of Yixing Public Security Bureau — dispute over termination of investigation decision

【Ruling Summary】

When applying a catch-all provision, an administrative agency must relate it to the circumstances already explicitly enumerated in the same clause, and determine whether the catch-all provision can be applied by reference to the standards established by those explicitly enumerated circumstances. The circumstances for applying the catch-all provision must be of the same or similar value as the circumstances already explicitly enumerated in the same clause, be consistent in nature and degree of impact, and conform to the legislative purpose of that clause.

Where "evidence is insufficient," the possibility of making a new administrative penalty decision in the future cannot be excluded. This situation does not have the same or similar nature as the circumstances for terminating investigation listed in items (1) through (3) of the first paragraph of Article 233 of the Procedural Regulations of Public Security Organs for Handling Administrative Cases (before amendment), and therefore does not fall under "other circumstances requiring termination of investigation."

Plaintiff: Ji Pin, male, born March 1, 1973, Han Chinese, residing in Yixing City, Jiangsu Province.

Defendant: Yicheng Police Station of Yixing Public Security Bureau, domiciled at Jianshe New Village, Yicheng Street, Yixing City, Jiangsu Province.

Legal Representative: Zhu Lianghong, Director of the Police Station.

Third Parties: Shen Zhanliang, male, born February 12, 1962, Han Chinese, residing in Yixing City, Jiangsu Province.

Third Party: Shen Tao, male, born February 18, 1986, Han Chinese, residing in Yixing City, Jiangsu Province.

Plaintiff Ji Pin, dissatisfied with the decision to terminate the case investigation made by Defendant Yicheng Police Station of Yixing Public Security Bureau (hereinafter referred to as Yicheng Police Station), filed an administrative lawsuit with the Jiangyin People's Court of Jiangsu Province.

Plaintiff Ji Pin's Allegations: Shen Zhanliang and Shen Tao, together with some social youths, forcibly entered his home and, without cause, beat him and his family members with weapons, causing him to lose consciousness on the spot. His relatives immediately called the police. Although Yicheng Police Station dispatched officers to the scene on the same day, they did not bring Shen Zhanliang and others to justice. On August 4, 2017, Yicheng Police Station issued a decision to terminate the case investigation, Yi Gong (Cheng) Xing Zhong Zhi Zi [2017] No. 1 (hereinafter referred to as the Termination Decision), on the grounds of "insufficient evidence and expiration of the case-handling period," deciding to terminate the investigation. He did not accept the Termination Decision and therefore filed a lawsuit with the court. During the trial of this case, Ji Pin amended his claims to: 1. Revoke the Termination Decision made by Yicheng Police Station; 2. Order Yicheng Police Station to perform its statutory duties and continue to investigate and handle the report made by his relatives; 3. The litigation costs of this case shall be borne by Yicheng Police Station.

Defendant Yicheng Police Station's Defense: The Termination Decision it made was based on clear facts, lawful procedures, and correct application of law. Shen Zhanliang, Shen Tao, and others had a physical altercation with Ji Panhong, Ji Pin, and others, during which Ji Pin was injured in the push and shove. After receiving the report, it immediately dispatched police to the scene to understand the situation, separately interviewed Ji Panhong, Shen Zhanliang, Shen Tao, and others, and made records. Subsequently, the Material Evidence Identification Office of Yixing Public Security Bureau conducted an injury assessment on Ji Pin, and the expert opinion clearly stated that Ji Pin's injury was minor. On January 25, 2017, after filing the case, it summoned Shen Zhanliang, Shen Tao, and others to make interview records. In July of the same year, Ji Pin and his mother Min Weijin, after two lawful summonses, refused to come to the police station for interviews without justifiable reasons. On August 4 of the same year, it made the Termination Decision in accordance with the provisions of Article 233, Paragraph 1 of the Procedural Regulations of Public Security Organs for Handling Administrative Cases (hereinafter referred to as the Procedural Regulations before amendment). It believes that it actively performed its statutory duties, promptly carried out work after the incident, fully investigated and collected evidence, but Ji Pin and his mother Min Weijin did not cooperate and failed to come to the police station for interviews. As the case-handling period expired and the existing evidence was insufficient to prove that Shen Zhanliang and others had illegal acts, the Termination Decision was correct. It requests the court to reject Ji Pin's claims.

Third Parties Shen Zhanliang and Shen Tao's Statements: They did not have any illegal acts, and request the court to reject Ji Pin's claims.

The First Instance trial by Jiangyin People's Court of Jiangsu Province found the following facts:

At around 9:00 a.m. on January 11, 2017, Shen Zhanliang, Shen Tao, and non-party Xu Feng went to Ji Pin's home to demand payment of a debt (deposit) from his father Ji Panhong (Ji Pin lived with Ji Panhong). The two sides argued in Ji Panhong's room. Upon hearing the argument, Ji Pin, Min Weijin, and Ji Fei entered the room, and a physical altercation ensued. Ji Pin was injured and taken to the hospital for treatment. On the same day, after receiving a report from Ji Fei, Yicheng Police Station dispatched officers to the scene to handle the matter. On the same day, it summoned Ji Panhong, Shen Zhanliang, and Shen Tao separately for interviews and investigations. On January 15 and 22, 2017, Yicheng Police Station interviewed Ji Fei and Ji Pin respectively.

On January 27, 2017, Yicheng Police Station registered and filed the case based on the preliminary investigation. On February 2, 2017, Yicheng Police Station interviewed Xu Feng. On June 30 and July 1, 2017, Yicheng Police Station again interviewed and verified with Shen Zhanliang and Shen Tao respectively. On July 4, Yicheng Police Station obtained approval to extend the case-handling period by 30 days. On July 5, 2017, Yicheng Police Station interviewed non-party Shi Guoping. On August 4, 2017, Yicheng Police Station made the Termination Decision, finding that the case of Ji Pin being intentionally injured had insufficient evidence and the case-handling period had expired. Pursuant to Article 233, Paragraph 1 of the Procedural Regulations before amendment, it decided to terminate the investigation. The Termination Decision was served on Ji Pin the next day.

During the first instance trial of this case, Yicheng Police Station clarified that the legal basis for making the Termination Decision was Item (4) of Article 233, Paragraph 1 of the Procedural Regulations before amendment, i.e., "other circumstances requiring termination of investigation." Because the facts could not be ascertained within the statutory case-handling period and the relevant persons did not cooperate, the evidence for finding illegal acts was insufficient, therefore Yicheng Police Station decided to terminate the investigation.

Separately, it was found that on January 17, 2017, Yicheng Police Station commissioned the Material Evidence Identification Office of Yixing Public Security Bureau to conduct a forensic medical examination on the extent of Ji Pin's physical injury. On June 12, 2017, the Material Evidence Identification Office of Yixing Public Security Bureau issued a forensic medical expert opinion concluding that Ji Pin's injury constituted minor injury.

According to the video data from body-worn cameras provided by Yicheng Police Station, in July 2017, Yicheng Police Station summoned Ji Pin and Min Weijin to the police station for interviews and investigations. When the summons was served at their home, Ji Panhong stated that Yicheng Police Station had previously notified them by phone to come, but the police officers did not make records, and he believed that the case handlers were not enforcing the law fairly. Ji Pin and Min Weijin did not again go to the police station for interviews.

The First Instance trial by Jiangyin People's Court of Jiangsu Province held:

The dispute in the first instance was whether "insufficient evidence and expiration of the case-handling period" constitutes "other circumstances requiring termination of investigation," and whether the application of the catch-all provision in the Termination Decision was correct.

In accordance with the relevant provisions of the Public Security Administration Punishments Law of the People's Republic of China and the Procedural Regulations before amendment, Yicheng Police Station has the duty to investigate and handle reports and accusations received within its jurisdiction.

Article 233, Paragraph 1 of the Procedural Regulations before amendment provides: "After investigation, if an administrative case has any of the following circumstances, the investigation shall be terminated with the approval of an officer at or above the level of the head of a police station, the case-handling department of a county-level public security organ, or an immigration border inspection authority: (1) no illegal facts exist; (2) the statute of limitations for the illegal act has expired; (3) the suspect of the illegal act is deceased; (4) other circumstances requiring termination of investigation." According to this provision, during the process of handling public security administrative cases, if it becomes unnecessary or impossible to continue the investigation, the public security organ shall promptly terminate the case investigation. Termination of investigation is a form of case closure. Where a legal provision uses an enumerative listing, when an administrative agency exercises discretion to apply a catch-all provision, it must be of the same or similar value as the definitive provisions within the same clause, consistent in nature and degree of impact with the acts already explicitly enumerated in the same clause, conform to the legislative purpose, and must not be applied arbitrarily. The circumstances identified by Yicheng Police Station for terminating the investigation were "insufficient evidence and expiration of the case-handling period," which are clearly not similar or comparable to the enumerated circumstances.

In summary, Yicheng Police Station, on the grounds of insufficient evidence and expiration of the case-handling period, based its Termination Decision on Item (4) of Article 233, Paragraph 1 of the Procedural Regulations before amendment. The reasons were clearly improper, and the application of laws and regulations was erroneous. The decision should be revoked in accordance with the law. In accordance with Items (2) and (6) of Article 70 of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, Jiangyin People's Court of Jiangsu Province rendered the following judgment on February 11, 2019:

1. Revoke the Termination Decision made by Yicheng Police Station.
2. Order Yicheng Police Station to make a new decision within 60 days from the date this judgment takes legal effect.

Dissatisfied with the first instance judgment, Yicheng Police Station appealed to the Wuxi Intermediate People's Court of Jiangsu Province, requesting the appellate court to set aside the original judgment, remand for retrial, or modify the judgment to reject Ji Pin's claims.

Appellant Yicheng Police Station's Appeal Reasons: 1. "Insufficient evidence and expiration of the case-handling period" as a reason for terminating the investigation was not improper. The real meaning of "insufficient evidence and expiration of the case-handling period" was that, as the statutory case-handling period was about to expire, due to the objective obstacle of Ji Pin's side not cooperating with the investigation, the existing evidence was insufficient either to punish or not to punish the individuals involved. Even if this reason for termination was poorly expressed in writing, it did not affect the actual reason for termination, which was "insufficient evidence." 2. The Termination Decision it made applied the law correctly. Articles 232 and 233 of the Procedural Regulations before amendment provided two forms of case closure: closing the case and terminating the investigation. The difference between the two provisions was that Article 232 deals with case closure when a decision on punishment or handling can be made against the actor, while Article 233 deals with case closure when no decision on punishment or handling can be made against the actor. The law grants administrative agencies discretion to apply catch-all provisions based on actual circumstances. The reason for terminating the investigation in this case was "insufficient evidence," not the absence of illegal facts, meaning that, considering the case circumstances, the possibility that the individuals involved had illegal acts could not be completely excluded. Therefore, its application of Item (4) of Article 233, Paragraph 1 of the Procedural Regulations before amendment to terminate the investigation had the same or similar value as the definitive provisions within the same clause, and the application of law was correct.

Appellee Ji Pin's Defense: The first instance found the facts clearly and applied the law correctly. He requests the appeal be dismissed and the original judgment upheld.

First instance Third Parties Shen Zhanliang and Shen Tao did not state any opinions.

Wuxi Intermediate People's Court of Jiangsu Province, upon second instance trial, confirmed the facts found in the first instance.

Wuxi Intermediate People's Court of Jiangsu Province held in the second instance:

Appellant Yicheng Police Station has the duty to investigate and handle reports and accusations received within its jurisdiction. Item (4) of Article 233, Paragraph 1 of the Procedural Regulations before amendment provides for "other circumstances requiring termination of investigation," which is a catch-all provision. The purpose of establishing a catch-all provision, as a legislative technique, is to avoid incompleteness of the law and to adapt to changes in social circumstances. However, when an administrative agency applies a catch-all provision through administrative discretion, it must not apply it arbitrarily. It should relate to the circumstances already explicitly enumerated in the same clause and determine whether to apply it by reference to the standards established by those explicitly enumerated circumstances. The circumstances for applying the catch-all provision must be of the same or similar value as the circumstances already explicitly enumerated in the same clause, be consistent in nature and degree of impact, and must conform to the legislative purpose of that clause. The three circumstances explicitly enumerated in Article 233, Paragraph 1 of the Procedural Regulations before amendment — "no illegal facts exist, the statute of limitations for the illegal act has expired, and the suspect of the illegal act is deceased" — are all determinate facts. The occurrence of such facts makes it impossible or unnecessary for the public security organ to take any further investigative measures in the case, meaning that such facts are sufficient to produce a final and irreversible effect of terminating the case investigation. Yicheng Police Station's termination of the investigation on the grounds of "insufficient evidence and expiration of the case-handling period" is clearly not of the same or similar value in nature and degree of impact as the circumstances explicitly enumerated in the above clause.

"Expiration of the case-handling period" is not a reasonable ground for terminating the case investigation, and "insufficient evidence" should not produce the effect of terminating the case investigation. Even if, as Yicheng Police Station stated in its appeal brief and during the second instance inquiry, the reason for terminating the case investigation — "insufficient evidence and expiration of the case-handling period" — was poorly expressed in writing and the actual reason for termination was "insufficient evidence," meaning that, considering the case circumstances, the possibility that the individuals involved had illegal acts could not be completely excluded, nevertheless, according to the principle of administration according to law, where there is insufficient evidence to prove the establishment of illegal facts by the individuals involved, Yicheng Police Station should have made a decision not to punish the individuals involved in accordance with Item (3) of Article 147, Paragraph 1 of the Procedural Regulations before amendment. If the public security organ subsequently discovers new evidence that allows the illegal act to be confirmed, it may, in accordance with Article 172, Paragraph 2 of the Procedural Regulations as effective from January 1, 2019, lawfully make a new decision and revoke the original decision not to impose an administrative penalty. Therefore, even if, as Yicheng Police Station stated, the actual reason for terminating the investigation was "insufficient evidence," Yicheng Police Station's decision to terminate the investigation was also without basis.

In summary, the first instance court, finding that the application of law was erroneous, rendered a judgment revoking the Termination Decision made by Yicheng Police Station and ordering it to make a new decision within a specified period. The findings of fact were clear, the application of law was correct, the procedure was lawful, and the conclusion was appropriate, and should be upheld. The appeal request of Yicheng Police Station lacks factual and legal basis and should not be supported by law. In accordance with Item (1) of Article 89, Paragraph 1 of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, Wuxi Intermediate People's Court of Jiangsu Province rendered the following judgment on June 26, 2019:

The appeal is dismissed, and the original judgment is affirmed.

This judgment is final.
